Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.vm

Interface Builtins

All Known Implementing Classes:
StandardLibrary
public interface Builtins
The part of a Mandela runtime that the machine knows nothing about.

The interpreter's job is names, frames and the operand stack. Everything that gives the language its usefulness — upper(), join(), json.encode(), reading a file, asking the host for a widget — lives in the standard library, and the library differs per host: the CLI has real files and a terminal, a Web Browser page has neither, an Espresso panel has its own console. So the machine never hard-codes a built-in name; when a member is not a declared field or method it asks this table, and when the table answers null it raises the AttributeError-style error the author sees.

One implementation is supplied by Runtime and is injected before the first run. Tests can inject a table with a single member in it, which is what keeps the interpreter testable without the standard library present.

  • Method Details

    • member

      Object member(Machine machine, Object receiver, String name)
      Resolves a member on a value that has no declared members of its own.

      Implementations must be cheap: this runs on the member-access path of every "list".join(", ")-style expression. The returned callable already knows its receiver, so the machine just calls it with the arguments the call site gave.

      The running Machine is handed over rather than stored: a library function that calls a script callback (map, sort with a comparator, a widget's handler) has to re-enter the machine that is executing it, and one library table is shared by every machine a host creates.

      Parameters:
      machine - the interpreter that is running this expression
      receiver - the value whose member is being read
      name - the member name
      Returns:
      a value, or a Callable to call, or null when there is none

    • importModule

      MandelaMap importModule(Machine machine, String path)
      Loads a sibling Mandela source file for import.

      The machine holds no filesystem knowledge — a page host has no files at all — so the request goes to the host, which is also the only party allowed to decide whether the path is reachable.

      Parameters:
      machine - the interpreter running the statement
      path - the literal path from the statement
      Returns:
      a map of the module's exported names
